plan.topic: Tirzepatide and the pancreas: how often pancreatitis showed up in randomized trials, what adverse-event databases can and can't tell us, and the label's warning signs (scoping review, Diabetes Metab Syndr Obes, Oct 23, 2026)
plan.angle: Calm 'honest uncertainty' Short, 170 words or fewer. Open with: 'Worried about your pancreas on tirzepatide? In randomized trials in people with obesity, pancreatitis was uncommon.' Fact 1: a scoping review (Diabetes, Metabolic Syndrome and Obesity, Oct 23, 2026) looked at 11 trials. Five reported pancreatitis, at rates from 0.2% (3 of 1,896 people) to 3.7%, and that 3.7% was 1 person in a trial of 27. Say 'in obesity trials' and don't apply it to type 2 diabetes. Fact 2: adverse-event report databases (FAERS, EudraVigilance) collect reports, but they can't tell you how often something happens. The authors call for standardized reporting. Warning signs, in label wording: severe stomach-area pain that won't go away, with or without vomiting, which may spread to your back. Then: 'contact your healthcare provider right away.' One line: nausea and diarrhoea are common. At most one gallbladder clause. Add 'Don't stop or change your medicines on your own', 'Not personal advice' and the full prescriber line. End with 'Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description.' No scare visuals and no emoji.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide and Your Pancreas: What the Trials Show #shorts
plan.why: Body-worry Shorts with tirzepatide in the title are our best Short format on YouTube (bones 237, nausea 153). A fresh Oct 23 review that no consumer outlet has covered yet gives it a new fact. | fact-check: Source confirmed: Kutsyba, Raj and van der Berg, 'Pancreatic and Gallbladder Adverse Events Associated with Tirzepatide in Obesity Management', Diabetes Metab Syndr Obes, Oct 23, 2026, doi 10.2147/DMSO.S637243. It is a scoping review of 11 RCTs, but only 5 of them reported pancreatitis. Rates ranged from 0.2% (3 of 1,896) to 3.7% (1 of 27). The 3.7% upper end is a single person in a 27-person trial. The review covers obesity only and left out studies done only in type 2 diabetes. Pancreatic and gallbladder events were reported more often in FAERS and EudraVigilance than in the trials. The authors call for vigilant monitoring and standardized reporting. Saying '0.2–3.7% across 11 trials' would misstate this. Also drop 'follow for more': the shared Shorts ending is 'Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description.'

package.description:
Pancreatitis was reported but uncommon in tirzepatide obesity trials: 0.2% on tirzepatide vs 0.2% on placebo in SURMOUNT-1. Adverse-event reports alone can't show true rates. Label warning sign: severe stomach-area pain that won't go away, which may spread to your back. If so, the label says stop using it and call your healthcare provider right away. Nausea and diarrhea are common. Otherwise, don't stop or change your medicines on your own.

Sources: Kutsyba et al., Diabetes Metab Syndr Obes, 23 Oct 2026 https://doi.org/10.2147/DMSO.S637243 | Zepbound Medication Guide https://pi.lilly.com/us/zepbound-us-mg.pdf

#Tirzepatide #Pancreatitis #GLP1 #ObesityTrials #PatientSafety
Not personal advice: talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

social.instagram_caption:
Worried about your pancreas on tirzepatide? Here's what a new scoping review of 11 obesity trials actually found.

In SURMOUNT-1, pancreatitis was reported in 0.2% on tirzepatide (all doses) and 0.2% on placebo.
One small trial reported it in 1 of 27 on tirzepatide vs 0 of 28 on placebo — the highest rate seen, in a tiny sample.
Most trials enrolled people without diabetes.
FDA and European adverse-event databases logged hundreds of pancreas/gallbladder reports, but raw reports can't show how often this actually happens.

Save this so you know the label's warning sign: severe stomach-area pain that doesn't go away (with or without vomiting, possibly spreading to your back). If that happens, the label says stop the medicine and call your healthcare provider right away. Nausea and diarrhea are common side effects.

Otherwise, don't stop or change your medicines on your own.

Share this with someone on tirzepatide who's wondered about this.

factcheck.summary:
I checked every source this Short cites, and they all exist. Most numbers match. One spoken number is wrong, so the verdict is REVISE.

**The error:** s3 says "Five reported cases". The scoping review (Kutsyba et al., DMSO, 23 Oct 2026) reports 11 participants with pancreatitis across five of the 11 trials. The script turned "five trials" into "five cases".

**What checks out:**
- **SURMOUNT-1:** Lilly Medical Information gives 1 adjudicated case (0.2%) in each tirzepatide dose and 1 (0.2%) on placebo. That's 3 of 1,896 versus 1 of 643, so the 0.2% versus 0.2% is right.
- **NCT04081337 (s4):** 55 people, type 2 diabetes excluded, 15 mg, 1 of 27 versus 0 of 28. The 3.7% is the review's highest figure.
- **"Most trials enrolled people without diabetes":** 8 of the 11 did.
- **"Hundreds" of reports (s5):** EudraVigilance has 363 pancreatitis reports. FAERS has 288 pancreatic and 249 gallbladder reports.
- **Reports aren't rates (s5):** the FDA FAQ says this data "cannot be used to calculate the incidence" of an adverse event.
- **Warning signs (s6):** the wording matches the Zepbound Medication Guide. I couldn't read the PDF itself (the page fetch couldn't parse it), so this is checked against my knowledge of the label, not the file.

**Smaller fixes:**
- In s7, "Otherwise" right after the side-effect line is confusing.
- The script runs to about 177 words, over the 170 limit.
- It's missing the label's caveat for people with a past history of pancreatitis.

issues.problem: The review reports 11 participants with pancreatitis across five randomized trials, not five cases. This undercounts the cases on screen and in the voiceover.
issues.fix: Eleven cases, across five of those trials. In SURMOUNT-1: zero point two percent on tirzepatide, all doses. Placebo: also zero point two percent.

issues.problem: With the sound off, viewers can't tell the tirzepatide figure pools all doses, and the 11-case total never appears on screen.

issues.claim: Nausea and diarrhoea are common. Otherwise, don't stop or change your medicines on your own.
issues.problem: Coming straight after the side effects, "Otherwise" reads as if nausea or diarrhoea were a reason to stop. It is meant to refer back to the label's pancreatitis instruction in s6.
issues.fix: Common side effects include nausea and diarrhoea. Apart from those warning signs, don't stop or change your medicines on your own. Not personal advice: talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you. Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description.

hold_reason: Dropped by Editor-in-Chief: The narration still says "five reported cases" of pancreatitis. The cited scoping review reports 11 cases across 5 trials. On a safety Short, an uncorrected, reassuring wrong number is a major factual error a viewer would be misled by. Fix scene 3 (plus the "Otherwise" wording, the past-pancreatitis line and the word count) and resubmit. Captions and audio are otherwise fine.

notes: Caption card ends on the orphaned word 'POINT' ('POINT TWO PERCENT'), which the style guide explicitly bans.
Pink circular cell pattern with flame icons is visually busy and slightly alarming without a clear focal point; the small blue pancreas icon at bottom gets lost against it.
In the second frame the word 'TWO' in 'TWO PERCENT.' renders faded/grey while 'PERCENT.' is solid white — looks like a leftover transition ghost rather than clean text.
Caption card ends on the banned orphan word 'POINT' ('WAS THREE POINT'), splitting the number '3.7%' across cards against the number-matching rule.
Caption ends mid-clause on 'AND NONE OUT', an awkward break that doesn't read as a full phrase in isolation.
Composition is a bit cluttered: adult+child mascot, speech bubble, extra small icon and three background figures compete for attention.
Caption spells out the abbreviation as spaced letters 'F D A' instead of 'FDA', breaking the spaced-letter rule.
Caption 'LOGGED HUNDREDS OF PANCREAS' reads as an awkward, incomplete/odd phrase (hundreds of pancreas, not 'pancreas reports').
Caption card ends on 'BUT REPORTS LIKE', an orphaned, incomplete phrase that doesn't resolve until the next card.
Caption card ends on the banned word 'THE' ('SO HERE ARE THE'), an explicit no-go per the style guide.
A small empty grey speech-bubble shape floats top-right with no text or tail pointing to a speaker — reads as a leftover placeholder bubble.
Caption card ends on a trailing comma ('FULL BREAKDOWN ON OUR CHANNEL,'), which the style guide bans.

audio.soundNotes: Music is already close to target (-13.5 dB under voice, -13.8 in pauses); nudged gain to 0.9 to stay gently under the voice given the serious adverse-event/warning-signs subject matter and 92% speaking ratio. Thinned the stacked transition cluster at 17.3s (dropped a redundant swoosh) and the 5-effect chip reveal at ~60s (dropped the quietest tick); pulled down a couple of speech-bed cues that read a touch loud (18.35s bubble, 22.2s swoosh, 39.5s pop/whoosh pair) and rescued the oddly buried swell at 55.8s. Added three bespoke, subtle cues (heartbeat intro, calm alert chime at the warning-signs reveal, and a soft ringtone blip at the "call your provider" label) to add felt emotional texture without competing with the narrator.
